{{Short description|Mathematical artwork}}
{{Orphan|date=August 2024}}

[[File:A Bird in Flight by Hamid Naderi Yeganeh.jpg|thumb|300x300px|A version of ''A Bird in Flight'' made up of 500 line segments]]
[[File:A Bird in Flight by Hamid Naderi Yeganeh 2016.jpg|300px|thumb|Another version of ''A Bird in Flight'' made up of 20,001 circles]]
'''Bird''', also known as '''A Bird in Flight''' refers to bird-like [[Mathematics and art|mathematical artworks]] that are introduced by mathematical equations.<ref name=":4">{{cite journal |title=Von Formeln und Vögeln |journal=[[Spektrum der Wissenschaft]] |date=February 4, 2021 |volume=05/2021 |page=47 |url=https://www.spektrum.de/kolumne/freistetters-formelwelt-von-formeln-und-voegeln/1826563 |access-date=9 April 2022 |language=German |issn=0170-2971 |archive-date=7 February 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210207071721/https://www.spektrum.de/kolumne/freistetters-formelwelt-von-formeln-und-voegeln/1826563 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |date=November 2014 |title=Mathematical Concepts Illustrated by ... |url=http://www.ams.org/publicoutreach/math-imagery/yeganeh |access-date=April 3, 2022 |publisher=[[American Mathematical Society]] |archive-date=July 29, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190729162002/https://www.ams.org/publicoutreach/math-imagery/yeganeh |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |date=September 18, 2014 |title=Mathematical Works of Art |url=https://mcs.blog.gustavus.edu/2015/09/18/mathematical-works-of-art/ |access-date=April 3, 2022 |publisher=[[Gustavus Adolphus College]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |date=January 8, 2015 |title=This is not a bird (or a moustache) |url=https://plus.maths.org/content/not-bird |access-date=April 3, 2022 |publisher=[[Plus Magazine]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite speech |title=Avian Arithmetic: The mathematics of bird flight |first=Peter |last=Cavanagh |event=[[National Museum of Mathematics]]' Events |location=[[MoMath]] Online, NY, United States |date=March 5, 2021 |url=https://momath.org/civicrm/?page=CiviCRM&q=civicrm%2Fevent%2Finfo&reset=1&id=4699 |access-date=April 3, 2022}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Gustlin |first1=Deborah |title=15.4: Digital Art |url=https://human.libretexts.org/Courses/ASCCC/A_World_Perspective_of_Art_Appreciation_(Gustlin_and_Gustlin)/15%3A_The_New_Millennium_(2000_-_2020)/15.04%3A_Digital_Art |access-date=April 3, 2022 |website=[[LibreTexts]]|date=17 November 2019 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Mathematics Portal - IMKT |url=https://imkt.org/math-portal/ |access-date=April 3, 2022 |publisher=[[International Mathematical Knowledge Trust]]}}</ref> A group of these figures are created by combing through tens of thousands of [[computer-generated images]]. They are usually defined by [[trigonometric functions]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Antonick |first1=Gary |date=January 25, 2016 |title=Round Robin |work=[[The New York Times]] |url=https://wordplay.blogs.nytimes.com/2016/01/25/moriconi-round-robin/ |access-date=April 3, 2022}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Chung |first=Stephy |date=September 18, 2015 |title=Next da Vinci? Math genius using formulas to create fantastical works of art |work=[[CNN]] |url=https://edition.cnn.com/style/article/math-art/index.html}}</ref><ref>{{cite book |last1=Baugher |first1=Janée J. |url=https://mcfarlandbooks.com/product/the-ekphrastic-writer/ |title=The Ekphrastic Writer: Creating Art-Influenced Poetry, Fiction and Nonfiction |date=2020 |publisher=[[McFarland and Company, Inc., Publishers]] |isbn=9781476639611 |page=56}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |date=September 16, 2015 |title="A Bird in Flight (2015)," |url=http://www.ams.org/mathimagery/displayimage.php?album=40&pid=616#top_display_media |access-date=April 3, 2022 |publisher=[[American Mathematical Society]] |archive-date=May 2, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180502211656/http://www.ams.org/mathimagery/displayimage.php?album=40&pid=616#top_display_media |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Young |first=Lauren |date=January 19, 2016 |title=Math Is Beautiful |work=[[Science Friday]] |url=http://www.sciencefriday.com/articles/math-is-beautiful/}}</ref> An example of ''A Bird in Flight'' is made up of 500 [[Line segments|segments]] defined in a [[Cartesian coordinate system|Cartesian plane]] where for each <math>k=1, 2, 3, \ldots , 500</math> the endpoints of the <math>k</math>-th line segment are:
: <math>
\left(\frac{3}{2}\sin^7\left(\frac{2\pi k}{500}+\frac{\pi}{3}\right),\,\frac{1}{4}\cos^{2}\left(\frac{6\pi k}{500}\right)\right)
</math>

and

: <math>
\left(\frac{1}{5}\sin\left(\frac{6\pi k}{500}+\frac{\pi}{5}\right),\,\frac{-2}{3}\sin^2\left(\frac{2\pi k}{500}-\frac{\pi}{3}\right)\right)
</math>.

The 500 line segments defined above together form a shape in the Cartesian plane that resembles a bird with open wings. Looking at the line segments on the wings of the bird causes an [[optical illusion]] and may trick the viewer into thinking that the segments are [[curved lines]]. Therefore, the shape can also be considered as an [[Op art|optical artwork]].<ref name=":5">{{cite news|last=Mellow|first=Glendon|date=August 6, 2015|title=Mathematically Precise Crosshatching|work=[[Scientific American]] (blog)|url=http://blogs.scientificamerican.com/symbiartic/mathematically-precise-crosshatching/|url-status=live|access-date=August 11, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150925094554/http://blogs.scientificamerican.com/symbiartic/mathematically-precise-crosshatching/|archive-date=September 25, 2015}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=เมื่อคณิตศาสตร์ถูกสร้างเป็นภาพศิลปะ|trans-title=When Mathematics is Made into Art|url=https://www.faa.chula.ac.th/SelfLearningFaamai/detailform/119|url-status=live|access-date=2021-10-03|website=Faculty of Fine and Applied Arts|publisher=[[Chulalongkorn University]]|language=th|archive-date=2021-08-19|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210819233835/https://www.faa.chula.ac.th/SelfLearningFaamai/detailform/119}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Mellow |first=Glendon |date=August 6, 2015 |title=Mathematically Precise Crosshatching |work=[[Scientific American]] (blog) |url=http://blogs.scientificamerican.com/symbiartic/mathematically-precise-crosshatching/}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |date=March 23, 2016 |title="A Bird in Flight (2016)," |url=http://www.ams.org/mathimagery/displayimage.php?album=40&pid=684#top_display_media |access-date=April 3, 2022 |publisher=[[American Mathematical Society]] |archive-date=March 29, 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170329234641/http://www.ams.org/mathimagery/displayimage.php?album=40&pid=684#top_display_media |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Passaro |first=Davide |title=Matematica e arti visive: percorsi interdisciplinari fra matematica, arte e coding |url=http://maddmaths.simai.eu/archimede/matematica-e-arti-visive/ |access-date=April 3, 2022 |website=Maddmaths! |publisher=SIMAI Società Italiana di Matematica Applicata e Industriale}}</ref>  Another version of ''A Bird in Flight'' was defined as the union of all of the circles with center <math>\left(A(k), B(k)\right)</math> and radius <math>R(k)</math>, where <math>k=-10000, -9999, \ldots , 9999, 10000</math>, and
<div style=" line-height:6em;">
: <math>A(k)=\frac{3k}{20000}+\sin\left(\frac{\pi }{2}\left(\frac{k}{10000}\right)^7\right)\cos^6\left(\frac{41\pi k}{10000}\right)+\frac{1}{4}\cos^{16}\left(\frac{41\pi k}{10000}\right)\cos^{12}\left(\frac{\pi k}{20000}\right)\sin\left(\frac{6\pi k}{10000}\right),   </math>
: <math>
\begin{align} B(k)= & -\cos\left(\frac{\pi}{2}\left(\frac{k}{10000}\right)^7\right)\left(1+\frac{3}{2}\cos^6\left(\frac{\pi k}{20000}\right)\cos^6\left(\frac{3\pi k}{20000}\right)\right)\cos^6\left(\frac{41\pi k}{10000}\right) \\ & +\frac{1}{2}\cos^{10}\left(\frac{3\pi k}{100000}\right)\cos^{10}\left(\frac{9\pi k}{100000}\right)\cos^{10}\left(\frac{18\pi k}{100000}\right), \\ \end{align}
</math>
: <math>R(k)=\frac{1}{50}+\frac{1}{10}\sin^2\left(\frac{41\pi k}{10000}\right)\sin^2\left(\frac{9\pi k}{100000}\right)+\frac{1}{20}\cos^2\left(\frac{41\pi k}{10000}\right)\cos^{10}\left(\frac{\pi k}{20000}\right).   </math>
</div>
The set of the 20,001 circles defined above form a subset of the plane that resembles a flying bird. Although this version's equations are a lot more complicated than the version made of 500 segments, it has a better resemblance to a real flying bird.<ref>{{cite web |date=April 22, 2018 |title="A Bird in Flight" |url=https://www.futilitycloset.com/2018/04/22/a-bird-in-flight/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180423021644/https://www.futilitycloset.com/2018/04/22/a-bird-in-flight/ |archive-date=April 23, 2018 |access-date=April 3, 2022 |website=[[Futility Closet]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |date=8 December 2020 |title=수학적 아름다움, 프랙털 아트의 세계 |language=ko |trans-title=Mathematical beauty, the world of fractal art |work=Sciencetimes |url=https://www.sciencetimes.co.kr/news/%EC%88%98%ED%95%99%EC%A0%81-%EC%95%84%EB%A6%84%EB%8B%A4%EC%9B%80-%ED%94%84%EB%9E%99%ED%84%B8-%EC%95%84%ED%8A%B8%EC%9D%98-%EC%84%B8%EA%B3%84/ |url-status=live |access-date=April 3, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201208103131/https://www.sciencetimes.co.kr/news/%EC%88%98%ED%95%99%EC%A0%81-%EC%95%84%EB%A6%84%EB%8B%A4%EC%9B%80-%ED%94%84%EB%9E%99%ED%84%B8-%EC%95%84%ED%8A%B8%EC%9D%98-%EC%84%B8%EA%B3%84/ |archive-date=8 December 2020}}</ref>
